patches.value: finite nonnegative real diameter ediam(V_i), with its canonical ENNReal coercion

Put ρ_i=ediam(V_i) in the ambient metric; since ρ_i≤δ<∞, use its underlying nonnegative real in interval-length and η_i expressions and its canonical ENNReal coercion in Hausdorff-content sums. Positive powers commute with this coercion.

Let D=dim_H(E), F=E×[0,1]. First show 0≤D≤n<∞. Nonnegativity is part of the critical-exponent definition. If n=0, ℝ⁰ is a singleton and E is that singleton, so D=0. If n>0, compactness H002 implies boundedness: the open cover of E by radius-one balls has a finite subcover, so E lies in a bounded box. For every sufficiently small h>0, subdivide this box into at most C h^(−n) grid cubes, C independent of h, each of diameter ≤√n h. For every fixed real m>n the total m-power cost is at most C n^(m/2)h^(m−n), tending to zero. For any fixed scale δ>0, take h with √n h≤δ; this is a Nat-indexed δ-cover after appending empty sets, and its cost can be made arbitrarily small. Hence C_m(E,δ)=0 for every δ>0, so M008's exact supremum formula gives H^m(E)=0. Apply M012 at each NNReal exponent m>n to infer D≤m for every m>n; taking the infimum over these m gives D≤n. Fix arbitrary q>D, so q>0. M003 at the NNReal coercion of q gives H^q(E)=0. Unfold M008: this is exactly the supremum over positive scales of the infimum of Nat-indexed cover costs, so every scale content C_q(E,r)=0. To ensure the admissible class at any r>0 is nonempty, cover E by open balls of radius r/3 and use compactness to extract a finite subcover; their diameters are ≤2r/3, and appending empty sets gives a Nat-indexed r-cover. Thus for every γ>0 the zero infimum supplies an r-cover of q-cost <γ. Choose r_j↓0, r_j≤1, and γ_j↓0 with such covers. Each nonempty zero-diameter member in Euclidean space is a singleton. Enumerate these by a finite or countable list and replace the k-th by an open ball containing it, of diameter ≤r_j and q-power cost <γ_j2^(−k−1); the total added cost is <γ_j. Leave positive-diameter members and empty members unchanged. The resulting cover has all nonempty diameters d_i positive, d_i≤r_j, and q-cost <2γ_j. For each i partition [0,1] into N_i=⌈1/d_i⌉ closed intervals of length 1/N_i≤d_i; since d_i≤1, N_i≤1/d_i+1≤2/d_i. The products U_i×K_iℓ cover F, have diameter ≤√2d_i, and form a countable family (a countable union of finite families), which can be enumerated by ℕ with empty sets appended. Their total (q+1)-cost is at most 2(√2)^(q+1)∑d_i^q<4(√2)^(q+1)γ_j, and their diameters are ≤√2r_j→0. For every fixed δ>0, all sufficiently large j give admissible δ-covers of F, so C_(q+1)(F,δ)≤4(√2)^(q+1)γ_j for all such j; letting j→∞ proves that content is zero. Since this holds for every δ>0, M008's exact supremum formula gives H^(q+1)(F)=0. Apply M012 at NNReal exponent q+1 to get dim_H(F)≤q+1. Since this holds for all q>D, taking the infimum over q>D gives dim_H(F)≤D+1. For n=0, F is isometric to [0,1]; interval covers of mesh h have at most 1/h+1 members of diameter ≤h and total a-cost tending to zero for every a>1. Thus H^a(F)=0 for every a>1, M012 gives dim_H(F)≤a for all such a, and taking the infimum gives dim_H(F)≤1=D+1. Isometries preserve ediam, cover conditions and the exact M008 formula.

For D>0 fix 0<s<D. For a>0 define C_a(A,δ)=inf{∑'ᵢ ediam(Uᵢ)^a : U:ℕ→Set(X), A⊆⋃ᵢUᵢ and ∀i ediam(Uᵢ)≤δ}. Empty members have diameter zero and hence zero cost for a>0. In M008, the supremum over nonempty witnesses is the ordinary power for a nonempty member and zero for an empty member; thus its inner infimum is exactly this content and H^a(A)=sup_{δ>0}C_a(A,δ), with no normalization factor. If δ₁≤δ₂, every δ₁-admissible cover is δ₂-admissible, so C_a(A,δ₁)≥C_a(A,δ₂). The one-sided limit as scale decreases to zero therefore equals this supremum: positive scales are cofinal at zero and the contents are monotone in the stated direction. M001 gives H^s(E)=∞; hence for every finite K, all sufficiently small positive δ have C_s(E,δ)>K. Fix δ>0 and any countable δ-cover (Vᵢ) of F. Set ρᵢ=ediam(Vᵢ), Aᵢ=π₁(Vᵢ), Bᵢ=π₂(Vᵢ). Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz in the concatenated Euclidean metric, so diam(Aᵢ),diam(Bᵢ)≤ρᵢ≤δ. In formulas for interval lengths use the underlying real diameter ρᵢ; in ENNReal content sums use its canonical ENNReal coercion. Given ε>0 set ηᵢ=ε2^(−i−1)/(1+ρᵢ^s)>0, with ε and ρ_i interpreted in ℝ for this choice. If Bᵢ is nonempty it is bounded; extend its infimum/supremum enclosure by total width ηᵢ to obtain open Jᵢ⊇Bᵢ of length ≤ρᵢ+ηᵢ. If Bᵢ is empty choose any open interval of length ηᵢ. For every t∈[0,1] and x∈E, (x,t) lies in some Vᵢ, so x∈Aᵢ and t∈Bᵢ⊆Jᵢ. Thus the Aᵢ with t∈Jᵢ cover E at scale δ. From the infimum definition C_s(E,δ)≤∑'ᵢ1_{Jᵢ∩[0,1]}(t)ρᵢ^s pointwise on [0,1]. Put ν=volume.restrict([0,1]) on ambient Borel ℝ. For integration on all ℝ multiply the left side by 1_[0,1]; outside [0,1] it is zero and the right side is zero, so the inequality holds everywhere. Every Jᵢ∩[0,1] is Borel; its indicator multiplied by ρᵢ^s is measurable and AEMeasurable for ν. The ambient mass is ν(ℝ)=volume([0,1])=ofReal(1−0)=1 by the restriction definition and M011; thus ν is finite and ν([0,1])=1. Integrating the left side gives C_s(E,δ)·ν([0,1])=C_s(E,δ), by M010 applied to the measurable interval [0,1] and constant C_s(E,δ). M009's monotonicity then bounds this by the lintegral of the series. Apply M002 to interchange the ℕ-indexed sum and lintegral; countability and AEMeasurability were checked above. M010 gives each summand integral as ρᵢ^sν(Jᵢ∩[0,1]). For S=Jᵢ∩[0,1], restriction gives ν(S)=volume(S∩[0,1])=volume(S). Enclose S in a closed interval of length ≤ρᵢ+ηᵢ (for S empty any singleton interval suffices). M013 gives volume(S)≤volume of the enclosure, and M011 evaluates the latter as ofReal(length)≤ofReal(ρᵢ+ηᵢ). Consequently C_s(E,δ)≤∑'ᵢρᵢ^(s+1)+∑'ᵢηᵢρᵢ^s≤∑'ᵢρᵢ^(s+1)+ε, where powers and sums on the right are in ENNReal and ε is coerced from ℝ; the inequality uses ηᵢρᵢ^s≤ε2^(−i−1), whose sum is ε. For this fixed cover ε is arbitrary: if its (s+1)-cost is finite, taking ε↓0 yields C_s(E,δ)≤that cost; if infinite the inequality is immediate. Since it holds for every cover, taking the infimum over all Nat-indexed δ-covers gives C_s(E,δ)≤C_(s+1)(F,δ). As δ decreases to zero the left side diverges, so the right side diverges as well; by the exact M008 supremum/content formula H^(s+1)(F)=∞. Apply M001 with NNReal exponent s+1 to obtain s+1≤dim_H(F). This holds for every 0<s<D, so taking the supremum over these s gives D+1≤dim_H(F). NNReal coercions are used for dimension theorems and the corresponding real exponent in M008.

value.bindings: Apply M012 to E with NNReal exponent m for every real m>n, after the grid argument proves H^m(E)=0; then let m decrease to n.
hypothesis_checks: H^m(E)=0 implies the Hausdorff measure is not top, and ℝⁿ is an extended-metric Borel space; m is positive and represented by its NNReal coercion.

value.bindings: Apply M010 to the measurable set [0,1] and constant C_s(E,δ) in ENNReal for the left-side integral C_s(E,δ)·ν([0,1]).
hypothesis_checks: [0,1] is Borel measurable in ℝ and C_s(E,δ) is ENNReal.
